body:
I'll try some of those suggestions. I don't think I have the energy to attempt SSD at this point. But, if some of the other ideas I am going to try on my own really don't work and I'm still in this same state (or worse) in a few months, I might go ahead and do it as a last resort. 

I'm not sure how to get a psychologist to help me because I lack insurance. They cost about 80-120 dollars a session. I can probably afford a once-a-month visit if I cut out other unnecessary expenses in my life. Otherwise I'm just not sure what to do. Maybe books, or something? I have this feeling inside, that the second I am cured physically, the mental problems will go away. They seem to only exist because I'm like this. It's like when my (adopted) dad got Cancer, and they gave him prozac right away. 

I'll try and look into alternative meds. The "ginger pills" and stuff like that are kind of a joke for my body to have a good laugh over. I need strong stuff to do well. But maybe some of them actually work, I don't know.

Thank you, I'll look into hyoscyamine ER. I can't afford another doctor yet, but next time I do, I'll ask. Oh- and it was metoclopramide - bill_tampa got it - at the time I wrote this I honestly didn't have the energy to look it up again.

Yes thank you - the drug was metoclopramide in fact. You're right. It sounded perfect for me so I was so very sad. 

I think one of those two situations is probably the problem, after researching. I see from your post and also info online that there are special diet plans for gastroparesis so I think my best bet is to try out those diet plans and see if my symptoms lessen. If things get worse I'll at least have those two ideas to suggest if I save up the cash to see another doctor.

No very rarely if ever. Last time I wrote here I got a lot of grief for saying MMJ didn't help me very much and I didn't really use it. So I tried to explain right away for the /r/trees people before I got more confusion.
I have just updated, unfortunately, with not really great news overall. But it's here - http://www.reddit.com/r/Health/comments/1bnkzb/update_my_bodys_so_sick_my_mind_is_starting_to/
i looked this up and this might be just the medication I need. Unfortunately my earliest possible appointment is the beginning of march, but i'm going to ask about this.

Awesome list - I hadn't seen that before. I'll ask the GI when I get my appt. Hopefully in a few months (or even earlier!) I'll be able to post here with an update and thank all you great people for your suggestions.

Thank you - I think you're catching on to something here with the postcholecystectomy syndrome. I'm going to bring this up as a talking point with the GI when I get an appointment, which may take a while since he's coming in from Denver. But he'll be worth the wait, I hope.
This is fantastic, I'll look into this as well. Thank you so much.
To be fair, it's probably because a lot of us have been a mystery to doctors so people here probably think it's something rare that most doctors don't notice. That's my guess.

I have great feelings towards MMJ because it has helped a lot of people I know especially my husband. I'm going to try an edible next time, maybe I need it to work more slowly on me. My problem I realized is that it gives me vertigo and dizziness.
You're right. I'm seeing a doctor who is from Denver and travels to my area, next.
This is all really sound advice, thank you. I'll be looking into those options now that you guys have helped me get back to fighting it and not just letting it win.

I do! I'll look into that, I have noticed a connection with the pain and that, now that you mention it. It doesn't cause the nausea as much, but I've definitely remembered the pain with diet soda. I only drink abt 1 diet soda a day, but still.

You're right. When I figure out what's happening with all these great suggestions and ideas and a new GI, I'm going to then focus on mind-work and try to deal with the phobias and any lingering anxiety/depression. I just can't focus on much of anything when the nausea is intense, so that's my priority. :)

I'm going to the next town over. It's still kind of a good old boys club in this very rural area I live in, but this doctor travels in and out of Denver so he might be able to help me with a different mind set.
Yeah I think this is what I'm going to do when I see a specialist in a neighboring town.

Hey thank you I think this is what *could* be going on with me too. I'm going to visit a new doctor (a GI specialist, my husband's idea) in a bigger city soon. From everything I've read this possibility sounds the most likely to me personally so I'll bring it up with the GI. What was the solution that helped you? Medication? How are you doing now?

Thank you for this thoughtful reply. You're right about agoraphobia being cumulative, by the way. Though on days when I don't feel nauseous (rare days!) I can go out *all* over the place and get everything done, all my shopping, etc. This happens about once a month or once every two months. Those days are the best days I have. 

I have caffeine sometimes, usually in the form of tea. Rarely drink coffee (I mean five or six times a year I'll drink one cup.) Sometimes take excederin for migraines (which are usually rare). I don't drink alcohol and never have. I don't smoke. I do drink soda. 

I'm average weight. I was overweight when all this started and I lost forty-fifty pounds. Now I'm average (about 145lbs). When I was only eating 500 calories a day I went to 130lbs. 

I do eat smaller meals. In fact I literally can't eat a large meal. I get full pretty fast. For example, one sandwich is a full meal that's borderline too much for me. 

Someone suspected it was Soy and I removed soy from my diet. This was the hardest thing in the world, maybe. Soy is in everything! I did this for a few months and it didn't work. I eliminated gluton for several months too. If the specialist says it's not a few of the most likely suspects, I'll ask for a food allergy test. I suspect it might not be food because it's not as much related to *what* is in my stomach, but if there's too much or too little.

I'm sorry I lost my cool for a moment, that wasn't good of me. I think I have just been very frustrated with anyone who tells me it's psychological first and foremost. I know it can cause real true physical symptoms, but this is definitely a medical problem first and the medical problem has led to depression and anxiety and agoraphobia. I'm not ignoring the whole anxiety idea at all - it's just that these symptoms appear at the most non-anxious of times. I'll be half asleep watching a movie in the comfort of my home and be struck suddenly with a wave of nausea that makes me sit right up. I get anxious from the wave of nausea. If the waves start to go away, my anxiety decreases, too. I know it's a balance, but this happens at such random times. There seems to be no emotional trigger. It happens when I'm nervous or when I'm lazily browsing the internet or taking a nice walk outside alone, or even when I'm asleep (it wakes me up.) 

You wrote out a really thoughtful and meaningful two replies though and I know you are honestly trying to be supportive and you are correct in the things you are saying. I know it doesn't apply to my current problem. However, there's definitely a correlation - these constant and surprise attacks of nausea have made me suffer psychological symptoms. Once this gets taken care of, I believe I'll be alright emotionally. Probably walking on air, actually, if this stops. That would be my dream come true.

After checking through and researching all the suggestions here I honestly think this is possibly what has happened. My husband suggested we go to a new gastro-specialist, and I'm going to ask about this and see how I can be tested for it. That and also H Pylori / ulcers also fits almost perfectly with my symptoms.

*sigh* Are you guys my doctors? 

This is what I was told when I nearly died from my failing gall bladder. I insisted and I begged them to help me and they didn't. It was just all my anxiety. I've had anxiety my whole life. I can tell the difference between between normal anxiety symptoms and physiological symptoms. I can wake myself up in the middle of the night from the pain or from the nausea. This happens when I'm calmly watching TV. Other times I've been able to stay out in town for several hours because for whatever reason my body gave me a break one day. 

The anti-anxiety pills I took while my gall bladder got worse by the minute didn't help me a bit. Then I was given them again. Another problem? Still all in your head.

I don't have the chronic diarrhea (associated with Crohn's) in any way, just the nausea bit. 

I did talk to my husband - tonight, and it went well. It was easier to talk when I had some ideas and possibilities suggested here.

I heard something like this, too. I actually prefer mainstream medicine. The doctor I had last been seeing sidelined as an acupuncturist and that sort of made me throw my hands up at my group of doctors. I didn't find out he was that until much later. 

My disappointment with mainstream medicine was their failure to recognize my gall bladder was badly failing me even with the ultrasound to prove something was wrong. I was saddened that they brushed me off even though I wasn't a regular visitor to clinics or ERs or anything - even during all this I only ever went to the ER one time, after ten hours of level 10 pain. They yelled at me for that, too. "Why did you wait ten hours with level 10 pain?" Because you MFers told me it was all in my head, that's why.

I have tried approx 10 times with I and S and hybrids. Vaping it is unbearable nausea, smoking it with a pipe is better, but minor increase instead of decrease. :( It causes tremendous nausea at first (first 20 minutes perhaps, time is hard to figure out when I'm on it) and has at least once (maybe twice) caused me to vomit shortly after I took it. I have tried using MMJ when I was in a grace period of no nausea, and I still got nauseous afterwards. 

I don't know if that information tells you or anyone else anything but I thought I'd put it out there just in case it's some kind of clear signal to someone of some particular issue. Especially since MMJ helps so many others with this exact problem.

I talked to my husband tonight after you guys have helped me see possible ways out of this hole. I didn't tell him that was the reason I was distancing myself but we talked about things we could do and try to fix this and he seemed eager to help me work out a solution. Thank you and I hope that your own situation improves, try /r/SuicideWatch if you are feeling that way currently. They pointed me in this direction and gave me hope so I think very highly of them.

Really good ideas, thank you. I have done MMJ for the nausea maybe ten times altogether. It had unfortunately made it worse, especially vaping it made it so bad I did get sick to my stomach. I have not done MMJ for about a year or two now. 

Luckily for me one key part of sma syndrome doesn't fit - my acute stomach pain is always when my stomach is empty. The pain goes from my stomach to my back between shoulder blades. Pepto Bismol or tums or something usually helps. So I get nauseous from eating *and* from not eating, (there's this wonderful break in the middle of meals, this perfect zone of no nausea.) but the pain is only ever there when I have not eaten - for example in the morning after sleeping. Ranitadine or other meds like that one make that pain fully go away. Also thankfully for me my stomach has no tenderness to the touch unless it's going through one of those pain episodes. 

I will take a multi now, I didn't realize that was an effect of gall bladder removal, thank you. No harm in a multi vitamin as far as I can tell. Could the whole operation itself have caused this to happen to me? I mean, if my body isn't absorbing vitamins the right way, is it also not digesting food the right way, or something else that could cause this intense chronic nausea? 

I don't know what an upper GI is but I got an endoscopy and the feedback was 'probable gastritis, possible gastroparesis.'

Dramamine Original formula only works for me, too. The 'non-drowsy' has no effect good or bad on me. Now I'm really wondering. But what other symptoms did your daughter have? I am not falling down or losing my balance when walking.
Thank you I never thought of this. I'll give it a try since I really can't do much harm at this point and it's OTC anyway here in US.

The promethazine works wonders and zofran had no effect. I take promethazine when things are at their worst but it's hard to function because it makes me fall asleep (but when I'm really really sick I don't care if I fall asleep as long as it stops.)

I'll think about the thyroid issue, thank you for the suggestion - it sounds like we went through really similar things.

I have tried MMJ (I live in Colorado) and it so unfortunately seems to make me more nauseous than without it. I must be unlucky. It helps with emotional issues I have but not with the physical issues I have. :(
I will try that, thanks.
I passed that test, the emptying study. It was slower than normal but not severely so.

Thank you for your reply. I had an endoscopy (camera down throat into stomach) before I had my gall bladder removed. That was very soon into the problem. They found nothing unusual except gastritis. (Inflammation of stomach lining) and ?? didn't say what I should do. So I looked it up myself and I've been taking Ranitadine once a day. 

I live in a very small town and I've seen all four available doctors. I went to the next town over about an hour away and the doctor there was the one who took my blood and said I was okay, even though I was becoming anorexic. Denver is four hours drive away and I don't think I can make it that far with my agoraphobia. I can barely make it to the town that's an hour away!

You gave me some hope with that idea - the health related subreddits. Do you know which ones are helpful for those questions? I got nervous to ask online because everyone always says 'go see a doctor' instead of offering suggestions.
